metadata.content:
The snippets you posted don't show the root cause yet. They only confirm:


startProject.ts launches the dev server.


registry.ts only tracks runtime state and logs.


Neither file explains why AI Preview renders correctly while Designer and Dev show a white page.


Given the symptoms from the previous investigation:


AI Preview works.


Designer canvas is blank.


Dev canvas is blank.


Browser viewport values are abnormal:
JavaScriptinnerHeight: 359
outerHeight: 949
ratio: 2.64


This occurs only in certain panels.


That strongly suggests a frontend rendering/container issue, not runtime startup.
Before changing runtime code, inspect the actual browser DOM.
Open DevTools in the blank Designer page and run:
JavaScriptdocument.querySelector("#__next")?.getBoundingClientRect()
JavaScriptdocument.querySelector("main")?.getBoundingClientRect()
JavaScript[...document.querySelectorAll("iframe")].map(x => ({
  src: x.src,
  width: x.clientWidth,
  height: x.clientHeight,
  display: getComputedStyle(x).display,
  visibility: getComputedStyle(x).visibility,
  position: getComputedStyle(x).position
}))
JavaScriptdocument.body.innerHTML.includes("iframe")
Then inspect the React root:
JavaScriptdocument.querySelectorAll('[data-panel]')
JavaScript[...document.querySelectorAll('*')]
.filter(el => getComputedStyle(el).overflow === 'hidden')
.slice(0,50)
Also check whether the iframe itself is rendering:
JavaScriptconst f = document.querySelector("iframe");
f?.contentWindow?.location?.href
and
JavaScriptconst f = document.querySelector("iframe");
({
  rect: f?.getBoundingClientRect(),
  style: f ? getComputedStyle(f) : null
})
If AI Preview works while Designer and Dev don't, the most likely causes are:
Possibility A — iframe height collapse
Designer/Dev panel iframe height becomes 0px because of a flexbox/layout regression.
Typical symptom:
JavaScriptheight: 0
Possibility B — overlay covering iframe
An absolutely positioned overlay is sitting on top of the iframe.
Typical symptom:
JavaScriptdocument.elementFromPoint(
  window.innerWidth/2,
  window.innerHeight/2
)
returns some overlay div instead of iframe.
Possibility C — wrong preview URL
AI Preview points at:
http://localhost:<runtime-port>
Designer/Dev points at:
about:blank
or stale project URL.
Possibility D — zoom transform bug
The viewport values you reported earlier are unusual enough that a CSS transform or zoom calculation could be collapsing available height in only those panels.
Run:
JavaScriptgetComputedStyle(document.body).transform
JavaScriptgetComputedStyle(document.documentElement).transform
JavaScriptdocument.body.style.zoom
JavaScriptdocument.documentElement.style.zoom
Do not modify startProject.ts or registry.ts yet. The evidence still points toward the Designer/Dev UI layer rather than the runtime process layer.
Paste the results of the iframe inspection commands above. That will identify whether we're dealing with:


runtime failure,


iframe URL issue,


height collapse,


overlay obstruction,


or viewport scaling corruption.
